newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah steadies but hedging seen a worr.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah steadies but hedging seen a worr.

text.p: Although Indonesia's currency market was stabilising, analysts on Wednesday expressed concern about increased corporate hedging of rupiah exposure, which could weaken the unit.
The rupiah recovered to a high of 2,530 against the dollar on Wednesday morning before fresh pressure on the Thai baht spilled over and sent it back at 2,585 the close.
Currency dealers said the rupiah was on its way to recovery and was even seen trying to break the strong resistance level of 2,500 as wild swings in the baht reversed the trend.
The stock market staged a relatively strong recovery at the opening, with the composite index rising rapidly, before being slowed by sustained volatility in the foreign exchange market.
Nevertheless the composite index gained almost one percent to close at 718.19 points on Wednesday on the rupiah's early recovery and a bullish Wall Street overnight.
Spurts of dollar-buying were reported after the rupiah plunged on Monday, but confidence seemed to have returned.
"The rupiah has traded back. The baht had weakened quite a lot today and affected other currencies," said a market analyst with a U.S. investment bank in Singapore.
"The concern we have is that the pressure is coming from the onshore market and we are detecting a kind of shift in sentiment," the analyst said.
"Companies which in the past were not too worried about being long on the rupiah, earning interest, are now starting to be a bit worried because of the volatility.

"They could be hit with losses. We are seeing more interest on the corporate side to hedge in the longer-term like in the swap, (these corporates) swapped their rupiah exposure for dollar exposure and are basically paying interest rate differentials," he said.
But the analyst added there were also investors who thought the rupiah above 2,600 level was overdone.
"They come in to establish long rupiah positions. You have the two sides of the market right now," the analyst said.
But he added that the year-end forecast for the rupiah remained at 2,550 per dollar.
The rupiah posted its biggest single-day loss on Monday, plunging almost five percent to a historic low of 2,665 before recovering slightly to 2,640 at the close.
Monday's falls were greater than when the market succumbed to nervousness in July last year over the health of President Suharto and riots in Jakarta later that month.

However, the rupiah recovered with ease on both those occasions, reflecting offshore confidence in Indonesia. But that confidence has been shaken by speculative attacks on regional currencies in recent weeks, forcing de facto devaluations in the Thai baht and the Philippine peso.
"Sentiment is still very cautious and this may not be the end of the volatility," the bank analyst said.

"But the long-term view suggests rupiah depreciation will return to the four-to-five percent annual target. However, it may be a touch higher this year because of the weaker peso and the baht," he added.

The rupiah, which started the year at 2,363 per dollar, had depreciated about 9.35 percent by Wednesday's close, compared with the government's unofficial annual depreciation target of about four to five percent a year.
It depreciated less than four percent last year.
